land.text: Franche-Comté and Artois, with Flanders, Nevers and Rethel, inherited by Margaret III and Philip the Bold in 1384

successors.note: Cliopatria's Duchy of Burgundy row begins in 1385 (67,648 km2) and contains 90 of the county's 92 cells in 1384. The county itself went on under the dukes until 1678; the page 'ruled by a count from 982 to 1678'.

capitals.name: Dole
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Dole' with no years. The page has 'Dole's parliament was the political center' and a council and parlement at Dole 'during the reign of Phillip the Bold'; Besançon was a free imperial city, not the county's seat. Arras was Artois's capital (Artois page).

rulers.name: Joan II
rulers.title: Countess
rulers.note: 'Joan II had inherited the County of Burgundy' in 1315 and Artois in 1329; 'when she died in 1330, she bequested Artois and Franche-Comté to her eldest daughter, Joan III.' The list starts here because the pages opened give reign years for no earlier count (the County page: Otto III 1231-1238, Adelaide 1248-1279).

rulers.name: Joan III
rulers.title: Countess
rulers.note: Married Odo IV of Burgundy in 1330; the end year is the Philip I page's 'Count of Burgundy ... from 1347' (he 'succeeded his grandmother').

rulers.name: Philip I (Philip of Rouvres)
rulers.note: Count of Burgundy and Artois from 1347, Duke of Burgundy from 1349; died 21 November 1361.

rulers.name: Margaret I
rulers.title: Countess
rulers.note: 'Philip died without heirs in 1361', the county went to Margaret I, who 'bequeathed her estates to her son Count Louis II of Flanders' (1382).

rulers.name: Louis II of Flanders
rulers.note: 'Louis II died in 1384 leaving no male heirs.'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 982-1328: the county before Artois. 'The county was formed in 982 by count Otto-William, encompassing his domains in northern parts of the Burgundian realm'; it 'became known as Franche-Comté (the Free County)'. The Franche-Comté page describes the modern region (Doubs, Jura, Haute-Saône, Territoire de Belfort, 16,202 km2) and says nothing on the county's exact limits (it does not say whether Besançon, Salins or Belfort belonged), so the gazetteer region is a reading. The 1237 transfer of Salins-les-Bains to an 'autonomous Seigneurie' is not drawn (no end given).

region.text: his domains in northern parts of the Burgundian realm

ledger.note: 982: Count Otto-William forms the County of Burgundy. 'The county was formed in 982 by count Otto-William, encompassing his domains in northern parts of the Burgundian realm'; infobox 'ruled by a count from 982 to 1678'. The year is the page's; the land is the modern Franche-Comté as a reading.

1329: Artois passes to the Countess of Burgundy. 'Upon her death in 1329, Artois passed to her daughter by the Anscarid count Otto IV of Burgundy, Countess Joan II' (who 'had inherited the County of Burgundy' in 1315). A personal union, drawn as one state as Cliopatria does from 1333.

1330: Joan III marries Odo IV, Duke of Burgundy; the county passes with Artois to the house of the dukes. 'when she died in 1330, she bequested Artois and Franche-Comté to her eldest daughter, Joan III', who married 'Odo IV of Burgundy in 1330'; the County page has the personal union with the duchy 1330-1361.

21 November 1361: Philip of Rouvres dies and the county leaves the ducal house. 'Philip died without heirs in 1361' (County page); King John II 'claimed the duchy for the kingdom of France'; the county and Artois went to Margaret I, 'the second daughter of Joan' (Artois page), ending the union with the duchy.
1366: the name Free County of Burgundy becomes official. The Franche-Comté page: the name 'Free County of Burgundy' 'did not appear officially until 1366'.

1382: Margaret I bequeaths the county to her son Louis II of Flanders. 'Margaret I bequeathed her estates to her son Count Louis II of Flanders'; the Artois page has Artois going back to Flanders 'ruled by her son, Count Louis II in 1382'.

1384: the county passes to Margaret III and Philip the Bold and joins the Burgundian lands. 'When Margaret's father, the Count of Flanders, died in 1384, she and Philip inherited the counties of Artois, Burgundy, Flanders, Nevers, and Rethel'; 'In 1384 all Flanders, Artois and Franche-Comté finally became part of the vast, complex territory' of the Duchy of Burgundy (Artois page). The county itself lasted to 1678.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line of the county is dated on the five pages opened; its limits (Besançon, Salins, Montbéliard, Belfort) are not given, and Artois is drawn as the Cliopatria Artois shape. The Franche-Comté region is the modern one.

notes: Five pages opened (the budget). SHAPES: the four Cliopatria shapes are Franche-Comté plus the Cliopatria Artois shape, kept (verdict ok). Cliopatria starts them in 1333; the pages put Artois and the County of Burgundy in one hand from 1329 (Joan II). The Artois dossier (eu-10) ends in 1332 per Cliopatria and logs the cells passing to this row in 1333, so Artois is drawn twice in 1329-1332; the renderer should prefer this dossier from 1329 or the Artois dossier should end in 1328. EXTENT BEYOND CLIOPATRIA: the dossier runs 982-1384, the page's 982 and Cliopatria's end. The land of 982-1332 sits in Cliopatria's Holy Roman Empire Minor States shape (60 cells cut out in 1333) and, for the Burgundy strip, in Kingdom of Arles shapes (which the Arles dossier marks wrong): a renderer must give this dossier priority there. After 1384 the county continued under the Burgundian dukes, the Habsburgs and Spain until the France-Spain transfer of 1678 (County page); that land is drawn by the duchy-of-burgundy dossier and later states, not here. NOT DRAWN: the 1237 exchange that made Salins an autonomous seigneurie (no end given); the 1295 cession of the county to Otto IV's daughter with the King of France as administrator; the 1032 inheritance of the Kingdom of Arles by Conrad II (the county becomes an Empire fief); the 1347 and 1349 accessions of Philip of Rouvres. DISAGREEMENT: the County page's infobox puts the personal union of Philip the Bold with the duchy in 1384 while its body gives 1330-1361 and 1405-1477, and the Margaret III page says Philip was granted the duchy in 1364 (so the union of 1384 is of the counties with the duchy already held by Philip); the Philip I page has the duchy 'claimed' by John II in 1361, Philip the Bold lieutenant-general 1363 and duke by June 1364. No war of 1333-1384 appears on the five pages, so `wars` is empty; the Hundred Years' War is not mentioned. The Cliopatria Flanders row (county-of-flanders, to 1384) shares the 1384 end.
